name: MO-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+21 partisan lean in a Missouri seat
Incumbent Mark Alford running with a large financial edge
Democratic challenger raised only ~$42k with no outside support
model.rationale: The district's R+21 lean, Alford's incumbency, and his roughly 33-to-1 fundraising advantage over Jordan Herrera leave no credible path for an upset, and markets agree at about 96% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings signaling vulnerability, the forecast stays firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: Any late independent spending or polling showing Herrera within single digits would be the first sign of a real race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mark Alford, the Republican incumbent in Missouri's 4th District, is seeking reelection in a seat with a strong Republican lean of about 21 points. He has raised nearly $1.4 million and holds over $747,000 on hand, while Democratic challenger Jordan Herrera has raised about $42,000 with minimal cash remaining. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but has shown no measurable activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, and prediction markets give Alford roughly a 96% chance of winning. The combination of district partisanship, incumbency, and the fundraising gap makes this one of the safest Republican-held seats up this cycle, with only a remote chance of a Democratic surprise.
